units.translation: ⟦1⟧: so also no oath of judges; cf. what Pylades says at ⟦2⟧. 622-624 Chorus. The Erinyes pretend that they cannot believe in such a command of Zeus (⟦3⟧, in contrast to Zeus), since father and mother would then be treated quite unequally. The argument is the same as that already put forward at 603. On ⟦4⟧ cf. ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧. ⟦7⟧ differently than at 747:

⟦1⟧ = ⟦2⟧, and it is rather to be compared with 423 ⟦3⟧, thus = to hold in no account. Wecklein cites ⟦4⟧: ⟦5⟧. 625-639 Apollo. The advocate now in fact maintains that the father and husband as such has greater claims to consideration, especially if he is such a one as Agamemnon, king and commander of the army. The spirited exposition, which at the same time brings out the treachery of the murder, but yet allows the main point, that it is his own wife who is the murderess, to recede very much into the background, is subject to what Cicero says in the Pro Milone (§ 17): non alio facinore clari homines, alio obscuri necantur: intersit inter vitae dignitatem summorum atque infimorum; mors quidem illata per scelus isdem et poenis teneatur et legibus; nisi forte magis erit parricida, si qui consularem patrem, quam si quis humilem necarit. 625
if he paid any heed to his father

⟦1⟧: as when a woman is killed. ⟦2⟧ belongs to ⟦3⟧ like ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧. On ⟦6⟧ see above on 15; ⟦7⟧ also ⟦8⟧ (⟦9⟧ according to Porson's emendation); besides only Pindar P. 8, 96, Frg. 137. The scholion must refer to this, that Epicharmus mocked Aeschylus for his constant use of this ⟦10⟧; for ⟦11⟧ is a ⟦12⟧. The ⟦13⟧ of the Pelopids already in Iliad B 100 ff.
627 ⟦1⟧ of a woman (not 'his wife'); ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧ are not rare in Aeschylus, e.g. ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧, ⟦6⟧ ⟦7⟧, roughly 'warlike'.
